This allows an attacker to send JSON with arbitrarily long numbers through the async parser API, leading to excessive memory allocation and potential CPU exhaustion, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

The standard synchronous parser correctly enforces this limit, but the async parser fails to do so, creating an inconsistent

Shaded async parsers in driver modules are other jackson-core versions (athena 2.15.2, databricks 2.17.1, snowflake 2.18.1, starburst 2.18.3, presto/druid 2.15.4), not this artifact.

facts.advisory_summary:
jackson-databind: InetSocketAddress deserialization triggers eager DNS resolution (SSRF) — ## Summary
`JDKFromStringDeserializer` constructed `InetSocketAddress` with `new InetSocketAddress(host, port)`, which performs eager DNS name resolution for hostname inputs at deserialization time. The fix uses `InetSocketAddress.createUnresolved(host, port)`, deferring DNS to an explicit connect.

facts.advisory_summary:
Apache HttpComponents Client: Connection Leak on Content-Encoding Decode Error Leads to Pool Exhaustion DoS — HttpClient based on the classic i/o model fails to correctly release the underlying connection back to the connection manager if it encounters an invalid or unsupported `Content-Encoding` header value in the response message. Please note this defect does not affect HttpClient based on the async i/o model.

This issue affects Apache HttpComponents Client: from 5.0-alpha1 through 5.6.2.

expect.note: Re-review majority (2 of 3 blind reads): httpclient5 5.3.1 sits in the main uberjar (META-INF/maven/org.apache.httpcomponents.client5/httpclient5/pom.properties). It has classic-client users: the ClickHouse driver module (clickhouse-jdbc 0.8.4, V2 is the default per ClickHouseDriver.class; client-v2 HttpAPIClientHelper builds the client with HttpClientBuilder and executeOpen and never calls disableContentCompression) and opensaml/shibboleth (SAML). The header-driven leak needs ContentCompressionExec to throw after chain.proceed, where InternalHttpClient.java:172 catches the HttpException without discarding the endpoint. In 5.3.1 the only throw is ContentCompressionExec.java:171-172 ('Unsupported Content-Encoding'), and it is guarded by !ignoreUnknown. HttpClientBuilder.java:907/910 always builds it with ignoreUnknown=true, and nothing else in the jar constructs ContentCompressionExec (only HttpClientBuilder and druid-jdbc's own shaded 5.4.1 builder reference it). BasicHeaderValueParser (httpcore5 5.2.5) never throws. Errors from decoding a bad body are raised lazily in LazyDecompressingInputStream, whose close() still closes the wrapped stream, so the connection is released. An unknown or invalid encoding is therefore ignored, not thrown, and the leak path cannot run in this version.

expect.note: Only tika-core is shipped (no tika-parser-pdf-module/tika-parsers in the jar; META-INF/maven/org.apache.tika has only tika-core). The `DigestAuthentication.apply()` method in Jetty's HTTP client uses `getBytes(StandardCharsets.ISO_8859_1)` at three locations (lines 171, 179, 196) to compute Digest auth response hashes. ISO-8859-1 silently replaces any character above U+00FF (Chinese, Japanese, Cyrillic, Arabic, Emoji, etc.) with 0x3F (`?`), causing all such characters to produce identical hash contributions. An attacker who knows a victim's username can bypass Digest authentication by repla

expect.note: Advisory targets DigestAuthentication.apply in Jetty's HTTP client; jetty-client is not in the uberjar (no org/eclipse/jetty/client/ entries). The server-side ee9 DigestAuthenticator exists but Metabase installs no SecurityHandler/LoginService: server is a ServletContextHandler with a proxy ServletHandler (src/metabase/server/instance.clj:113-123); no class outside Jetty references SecurityHandler/DigestAuthenticator. Auth is Metabase's own session/cookie logic.

facts.advisory_summary:
Jetty has HTTP Request Smuggling via Chunked Extension Quoted-String Parsing — ### Description (as reported)

Jetty incorrectly parses quoted strings in HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer encoding extension values, enabling request smuggling attacks.

### Background

This vulnerability is a new variant discovered while researching the "Funky Chunks" HTTP request smuggling techniques:
- https://w4ke.info/2025/06/18/funky-chunks.html
- https://w4ke.info/2025/10/29/funky-chunks-2.html

The original research tested various chunk extension parsing differentials but did not test quoted-string handling within

expect.note: Jetty 12.0.21 HTTP/1.1 connector parses every request (ring-jetty create-server, src/metabase/server/instance.clj:113-123, default port 3000). HttpParser CHUNK_PARAMS state ignores quoted-strings and ends the extension on the first LF (jetty-http HttpParser.java:1941-1961), so attacker chunked bodies with quoted chunk extensions hit the vulnerable parsing; smuggling needs a front proxy with differing parsing, but the code runs on unauthenticated input.

|---|---|---| --- |
| `http://[0:0:0:0:0:ffff:127.0.0.1]` | invalid | host=`[::ffff:127.0.0.1]` | host=`[::ffff:127.0.0.1]` | 
| `http://[:

expect.note: Re-review majority (2 of 3 blind reads): Metabase serves HTTP on embedded Jetty 12.0.21 (deps.edn:163-166; src/metabase/server/instance.clj:18-20), with jetty-http 12.0.21 in the uberjar. Every inbound request target, including absolute-form URIs with a scheme and authority/IPv6 literals, goes through HttpURI.build(method, uri) (jetty-server internal/HttpConnection.java:1122), which reaches the flagged parser (jetty-http HttpURI.java:1132 parse, SCHEME_OR_PATH at 1208 normalising whatever precedes ':' as the scheme, IPV6 at 1356). Unauthenticated remote clients therefore feed attacker-controlled URIs to this parser by default. The impact is only a parser differential (it matters when another component re-parses the same URI, for example request-URL reconstruction or proxies), but the vulnerable code runs on attacker input, so per the brief this is reachable.

facts.advisory_summary:
The Eclipse Jetty Server Artifact has a Gzip request memory leak  — ### Description (as reported)

There is a memory leak when using `GzipHandler` in jetty-12.0.30 that can cause off-heap OOMs. This can be used for DoS attacks so I'm reporting this as a vulnerability.

The leak is created by requests where the request is inflated (`Content-Encoding: gzip`) and the response is not deflated (no `Accept-Encoding: gzip`). In these conditions, a new inflator will be created by `GzipRequest` and never released back into `GzipRequest.__inflaterPool` because `gzipRequest.destory()` is not called.

expect.note: Leak is in GzipHandler/GzipRequest; Metabase does not install Jetty GzipHandler (server handler chain is ServletContextHandler + statistics handler + proxy ServletHandler, src/metabase/server/instance.clj:113-123; response gzip is ring-gzip-middleware, deps.edn:10). No class outside Jetty references GzipHandler.

A minimal example is:

In my local reproduction, URIUtil.canonicalPath() returns:

`/public/../admin/secret`

instead of the expected normalized path:

expect.note: URIUtil.canonicalPath leaving '..' after ';' matters only when a path-based security decision is made on the canonical path (SecurityHandler.PathMapped constraints). Metabase installs no SecurityHandler (src/metabase/server/instance.clj:113-123) and does its own authorization in ring handlers on the request map built from the servlet request (ring.util.jakarta.servlet build-request-map, instance.clj:68), so no constraint can be bypassed.

facts.advisory_summary: jsoup XmlTreeBuilder vulnerable to memory exhaustion through deeply nested namespace declarations — jsoup through 1.23.2, fixed in commit 862ba2f, contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in XmlTreeBuilder that allows remote attackers to exhaust JVM heap memory by supplying a deeply nested XML document with uniquely-namespaced elements. The builder copies the entire inherited namespace map on every start element, causing quadratic time and memory complexity, which attackers can exploit to trigger an OutOfMemoryError and terminate the application.

expect.note: Bug is in jsoup's XmlTreeBuilder (Parser.xmlParser). Top-level jsoup users are hickory (HTML parse, src/metabase/channel/render/preview.clj:143-147 hik/parse) and the Redshift driver's OktaCredentialsProvider (Jsoup.parse(String) HTML); no class outside jsoup references xmlParser/XmlTreeBuilder (Snowflake carries its own shaded jsoup). HTML parsing uses HtmlTreeBuilder.

facts.advisory_summary:

When a Java application connects with sslMode=verify-full (or verify-ca) and a password but does not pin a server certificate, Connector/J deliberately accepts an untrusted/self-signed certificate at the TLS layer (the "MITM-proof without a CA" feature) and proves the server's identity afterwards by binding the certificate fingerprint into the authentication exchange. That fingerprint enforcement is applied to the OK-packet and auth-switch paths but not to the initial-handshake path. An active man-in-th

expect.note: Advisory concerns the sslMode=verify-full/verify-ca 'MITM-proof without a CA' certificate-fingerprint binding. mariadb-java-client 2.7.10 (used by Metabase for MySQL/MariaDB, src/metabase/app_db/spec.clj:49-50) has no sslMode option and no fingerprint code (no 'sslMode'/'ingerprint' in its sources); TLS is useSSL/trustServerCertificate/serverSslCert (src/metabase/driver/mysql.clj:605-617), so the flawed feature does not exist in this version.

facts.advisory_summary:
org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client has Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information and Insufficiently Protected Credentials — ### Summary

When PAM (dialog) authentication is used, the connector can be coerced into sending the account password in cleartext over an insecure connection. A hostile or man-in-the-middle server can trigger this with the default configuration, disclosing the user's password.

### Details

The mysql_clear_password plugin is gated behind a secure connection: the driver refuses to transmit the password in cleartext over plain TCP. The sibling PAM plugin handler (S

expect.note: Metabase connects to MySQL/MariaDB (data warehouses and optional app DB) with org.mariadb.jdbc.Driver 2.7.10 (src/metabase/app_db/spec.clj:49-50; src/metabase/driver/mysql.clj:603-623). On an AuthSwitchRequest the driver loads whatever plugin the server names (AbstractConnectProtocol.java:736-749); SendPamAuthPacket ('dialog') is registered in META-INF/services/org.mariadb.jdbc.authentication.AuthenticationPlugin and does not override mustUseSsl, so a hostile/MITM server gets the password in cleartext over plain TCP (Metabase sets useSSL=false unless SSL chosen, mysql.clj:617).
expect.requires: a MySQL/MariaDB database connection (documented; admin adds it) or MySQL app DB

facts.advisory_summary:
org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client has Inappropriate Encoding for Output Context — ### Summary

The connector encodes and decodes all character data assuming the connection character set is UTF-8. A server can change character_set_client mid-session to a non-UTF-8 charset, after which the driver and server interpret the same bytes under different encodings, causing silent data corruption and a client/server charset-confusion mismatch.

### Details

The driver encodes and decodes all character data on the assumption that the connection character set is UTF-8. 
Charset can be changed by comman

expect.note: 2.7.10 encodes/decodes all character data as UTF-8 regardless of server character_set_client, and Metabase's MySQL connections force UTF-8 assumptions (useUnicode/characterEncoding UTF8, src/metabase/driver/mysql.clj:575-579; spec src/metabase/app_db/spec.clj:49-50). A hostile MySQL/MariaDB server (or native-SQL user issuing SET character_set_client on a pooled connection) can change the charset mid-session, after which client-side escaped parameters (dashboard filter values from users) are interpreted under a different encoding.
